question: For which of these is it acceptable to use hazard warning lights?
options: When parked on double yellow lines while shopping
When you want to thank another driver
When reversing into a parking space
When your vehicle has broken down and is causing an obstruction
explanation: Hazard warning lights. These may be used when your vehicle is stationary, to warn that it is temporarily obstructing traffic. Never use them as an excuse for dangerous or illegal parking. You MUST NOT use hazard warning lights while driving or being towed unless you are on a motorway or unrestricted dual carriageway and you need to warn drivers behind you of a hazard or obstruction ahead. (Highway Code rule 116.)

question: Unless signs show otherwise, what speed limit usually applies on a road with street lighting?
options: 30 mph
20 mph
40 mph
The national speed limit
explanation: You MUST NOT exceed the maximum speed limits for the road and for your vehicle. A speed limit of 30 mph generally applies to all roads with street lights unless signs show otherwise. The national speed limit for cars on single carriageways is 60 mph and on dual carriageways and motorways 70 mph. (Highway Code rule 124.)

question: You are on a road with a solid white line nearest to you. When may you cross it to overtake?
options: To pass a pedal cycle, horse or road maintenance vehicle travelling at 10 mph or less
Whenever the road ahead is clear
Never under any circumstances
Only at night when traffic is light
explanation: Double white lines where the line nearest to you is solid. This means you MUST NOT cross or straddle it unless it is safe and you need to enter adjoining premises or a side road, or to pass a stationary vehicle, or overtake a pedal cycle, horse or road maintenance vehicle if they are travelling at 10 mph or less. (Highway Code rule 129.)

question: An area of white chevrons on the road is bordered by a solid white line. What does this mean?
options: It marks a cycle lane
It is reserved for motorcycles
You may use it to overtake if safe
You MUST NOT enter the area except in an emergency
explanation: Areas of white diagonal stripes or chevrons painted on the road. These are to separate traffic lanes or to protect traffic turning right. If the area is bordered by a broken white line, you should not enter the area unless it is necessary and you can see that it is safe to do so. If the area is marked with chevrons and bordered by solid white lines you MUST NOT enter it except in an emergency. (Highway Code rule 130.)

question: When may you enter a box junction and wait?
options: When turning right and only oncoming traffic, or other right-turning traffic, is preventing you from completing the turn
When your exit is blocked but you can fit in the box
When the lights are about to change
When the traffic ahead is slow-moving
explanation: Box junctions. These have criss-cross yellow lines painted on the road. You MUST NOT enter the box until your exit road or lane is clear. However, you may enter the box and wait when you want to turn right, and are only stopped from doing so by oncoming traffic, or by other vehicles waiting to turn right. (Highway Code rule 135.)

question: A cycle lane is marked by a solid white line. During its hours of operation, what does this mean for drivers?
options: You may use it to overtake on the left
You may park in it outside rush hour
You MUST NOT drive or park in it
You may stop briefly to set down passengers
explanation: Cycle lanes. You MUST NOT drive or park in a cycle lane marked by a solid white line during its times of operation. Do not drive or park in a cycle lane marked by a broken white line unless it is unavoidable. (Highway Code rule 140.)

question: On a single-track road you meet an oncoming vehicle near a passing place on your right. What should you do?
options: Reverse until you find a passing place on your left
Sound your horn and continue
Drive onto the verge
Wait opposite the passing place so the other vehicle can enter it
explanation: Single-track roads. These are only wide enough for one vehicle. They may have special passing places. If you see a vehicle coming towards you, or the driver behind wants to overtake, pull into a passing place on your left, or wait opposite a passing place on your right. (Highway Code rule 155.)

question: In which situation MUST you NOT overtake?
options: When the vehicle ahead is travelling below the speed limit
On a one-way street
After a “No Overtaking” sign and before the sign cancelling it
On a dual carriageway
explanation: You MUST NOT overtake if you would have to cross or straddle double white lines with a solid line nearest to you, if you would have to enter an area designed to divide traffic, if you would have to enter a lane reserved for buses, trams or cycles during its hours of operation, the nearest vehicle to a pedestrian crossing, or after a 'No Overtaking' sign until you pass a sign cancelling the restriction. (Highway Code rule 165.)

question: At a junction with a STOP sign and solid white line, what MUST you do?
options: Stop only if traffic is approaching
Give way to traffic from the right only
Slow down and proceed if clear
Stop behind the line, even if the road is clear, then move off when safe
explanation: You MUST stop behind the line at a junction with a 'Stop' sign and a solid white line across the road. Wait for a safe gap in the traffic before you move off. (Highway Code rule 171.)

question: You are approaching traffic lights and the amber light shows on its own. What does it mean?
options: Stop only if pedestrians are crossing
Stop at the line — you may only continue if you have crossed it or stopping might cause a collision
Proceed with caution
Prepare to go — the lights will turn green
explanation: You MUST stop behind the white 'Stop' line across your side of the road unless the traffic light is green. If the amber light appears you may go on only if you have already crossed the stop line or are so close to it that to stop might cause a collision. (Highway Code rule 175.)

question: When reaching a roundabout you should normally give priority to…
options: Traffic approaching from your right, unless signs or markings say otherwise
Traffic on your left
Traffic already signalling left
Larger vehicles regardless of position
explanation: When reaching the roundabout you should give priority to traffic approaching from your right unless directed otherwise by signs, road markings or traffic lights. (Highway Code rule 185.)

question: You are taking the second exit (straight ahead) at a roundabout. When should you signal left?
options: You should not signal at all
As soon as you enter the roundabout
After you have passed the exit before the one you want
On approach to the roundabout
explanation: Signals and position when using a roundabout. When taking the first exit, signal left and approach in the left-hand lane. When taking any intermediate exit, select the appropriate lane, do not signal on approach, and signal left after you have passed the exit before the one you want. (Highway Code rule 186.)

question: Within the zig-zag lines at a pedestrian crossing you MUST NOT…
options: Park, or overtake the vehicle nearest the crossing
Drive faster than 20 mph
Stop to let pedestrians cross
Use your horn
explanation: You MUST NOT park on a crossing or in the area covered by the zig-zag lines. You MUST NOT overtake the moving vehicle nearest the crossing or the vehicle nearest the crossing which has stopped to give way to pedestrians. (Highway Code rule 191.)

question: Why does the Highway Code advise you to reverse INTO a driveway and drive OUT forwards?
options: So you can see clearly when joining the road
It is easier on the clutch
It is a legal requirement
It uses less fuel
explanation: Do not reverse from a side road into a main road. When using a driveway, reverse in and drive out if you can. (Highway Code rule 201.)

question: What does the Highway Code say about how far you may reverse?
options: No more than two car lengths
No more than 20 metres
There is no limit on quiet roads
You MUST NOT reverse further than necessary
explanation: You MUST NOT reverse your vehicle further than necessary. (Highway Code rule 203.)

question: What do double yellow lines along the edge of the road mean?
options: No stopping at any time
Loading only
No waiting during the hours shown
No waiting at any time
explanation: You MUST NOT wait or park on yellow lines during the times of operation shown on nearby time plates. Double yellow lines indicate a prohibition of waiting at any time even if there are no upright signs. (Highway Code rule 238.)

question: On which of these MUST you NOT stop or park (except in an emergency)?
options: The carriageway or hard shoulder of a motorway
A road with street lighting
A residential cul-de-sac
A road with a single yellow line outside its hours of operation
explanation: You MUST NOT stop or park on the carriageway or hard shoulder of a motorway except in an emergency, on a pedestrian crossing including the area marked by zig-zag lines, on a clearway, in a bus stop clearway during its hours of operation, on an urban clearway during its hours of operation, on a road marked with double white lines, in a tram or cycle lane during its period of operation, on a cycle track, or on red lines. (Highway Code rule 240.)

question: According to the Highway Code, you should NOT park within what distance of a junction (unless in an authorised space)?
options: 5 metres
20 metres
15 metres
10 metres (32 feet)
explanation: DO NOT stop or park near a school entrance, anywhere you would prevent access for emergency services, at or near a bus or tram stop or taxi rank, opposite or within 10 metres (32 feet) of a junction except in an authorised parking space, near the brow of a hill or hump bridge, opposite a traffic island, in front of an entrance to a property, on a bend, or where the kerb has been lowered to help wheelchair users and powered mobility vehicles. (Highway Code rule 243.)

question: At night, you MUST NOT park on a road facing against the direction of traffic flow unless…
options: You are within 10 metres of a junction
You leave your sidelights on
You are in a recognised parking space
The road has street lighting
explanation: You MUST NOT park on a road at night facing against the direction of the traffic flow unless in a recognised parking space. (Highway Code rule 248.)

question: When MUST you display parking lights when parked on a road at night?
options: Whenever it is dark
Only on dual carriageways
Only if you are within 10 metres of a junction
When the speed limit on that road is greater than 30 mph
explanation: All vehicles MUST display parking lights when parked on a road or a lay-by on a road with a speed limit greater than 30 mph. (Highway Code rule 249.)
